## 2026 event (current) — Improving Company Retreat, Las Vegas, Sept 29 – Oct 4, 2026

The real documents live in OneDrive (not the IES repo):

**`/Users/davidohara/Library/CloudStorage/OneDrive-Improving/Corporate/Retreat/2026/Amazing Race/`**

- **`2026 Amazing Race (Basic Rules).docx`** — Three categories: RED ENVELOPES = Power (up to 50 pts each, 6 stations across Fremont Street); BLUE = Quest (15–35 pts, group/seek-out activities); GREEN = Fortune (0–30 pts plus purse bonus, team-bank gambling). Key rules: only 1 Power envelope given at start; must start with Quest or Fortune; only top 3 Power scores count; one envelope open at a time (honor system); don't spend own money (team bank); keep score on card; total = points + bank remaining ÷ 10; "this is the playtest." **Questions go to the "Amazing Race Help Desk channel in Teams."**

Every station says "Use the Teams channel if you have any questions or need guidance on the location."

# 2. Teams / Microsoft Graph infrastructure

**No Graph API, az cli, or Teams webhook scripts exist anywhere.** All Microsoft access is via MCP connectors:

- **MS 365 MCP connector** (tool prefix `mcp__b8c41a14-7a9b-4ea5-ab12-933ee04bc52f__*`) with exactly four tools used across the repo: `outlook_calendar_search`, `outlook_email_search`, **`chat_message_search`** (Teams 1:1/group chat search — used by ~25 skills incl. shep-one-on-one, chief-prep, chase-client-prep), and `read_resource` (fetches transcript URIs, format `meeting-transcript:///<meetingId>`). In the current session this same capability is the **claude.ai Microsoft 365 MCP server** (`mcp__claude_ai_Microsoft_365__authenticate` / `complete_authentication`, tool list deferred).
- **`skills/teams-transcripts/SKILL.md`** (canonical, owning_agent: knox) and its Claude-facing wrapper **`.claude/skills/knox-transcripts-teams/SKILL.md`** — the full Teams pipeline: calendar search → `meetingTranscriptUrl` via `read_resource` → WebVTT parse → Obsidian note → OmniFocus routing. Companion: `references/vault-conventions.md`.
- **Teams channel monitoring: nothing exists.** The only Teams reads are meeting transcripts and `chat_message_search`. The 2026 Amazing Race docs themselves reference two channels with no tooling pointed at them: the **"Amazing Race Help Desk"** channel and the **"Vegas Teams/Photos"** channel (where all quest photos/videos must be posted, tagging Dawn Dearstone, with team number and quest number).
- Obsidian MCP (`mcp__obsidian-mcp-tools__*`) is configured in skills but **currently failing to connect** (ConnectionRefused) — the vault is also directly reachable on the filesystem at the iCloud path above.

# 3. Image-analysis / photo-review tooling

- **`.claude/skills/knox-photo-tag/SKILL.md`** — the main precedent: batch Apple Photos analysis (AppleScript reads, Claude vision via the Read tool's image rendering), keyword write-back through the macOS Shortcut "Tag Photo", M365 calendar events for event tags, a known-faces reference set, resumable state in `data/photo-pipeline/manifest.json` (gitignored). Runs as a sub-agent to keep vision calls out of main context.
- **`skills/visual-verification/SKILL.md`** (owning_agent: rigby) — hard human-approval gate: reads a screenshot with the Read tool, checks each value in a reference_context individually, explicit approval or logged escalation required. Consumed by `workflows/golf-booking/steps/step-05-visual-verification.md`.
- **`skills/peekaboo/` + `.claude/skills/peekaboo/`** — macOS screen capture / UI inspection via the Peekaboo CLI (screenshots and UI automation, not photo analysis).

# 4. IES structure conventions (agents/, workflows/, skills/)

- **Agents** — `agents/{name}.md` persona files (Metadata, Persona, Task Portfolio, Data Requirements, Priority Logic, Handoff Behavior). **`agents/conventions.md`** holds shared protocols: error reporting (`## Self-Corrections` blocks → Master logs to `systems/error-tracking/entries/`), working-memory write schema, tiered memory rules, output format hierarchy (HTML > Markdown > PDF > Office; vault-destined output is always Markdown), Slack notification handoff blocks, and file-naming conventions.
- **Skills** — dual location: `skills/{name}/SKILL.md` is canonical (frontmatter: name, owning_agent, description, model, trigger_keywords, trigger_agents, fairness) and `.claude/skills/{name}/SKILL.md` is the Claude-facing wrapper (frontmatter: name, description, context: fork, agent: general-purpose, allowed-tools, model; body delegates to the canonical file). Every skill must end with a **`## SKILL COMPLETE`** block (writes `systems/eval-harness/skill-runs/{skill}-latest.json`) and a **`## GRADE THIS RUN`** block (`python3 systems/eval-harness/grade_skill_run.py --skill {name}`). Registration: `skills/_index.md` and `skills/_manifest.jsonl` plus per-agent `_manifest-{agent}.jsonl`.
- **Workflows** — `workflows/{noun-verb}/workflow.md` (frontmatter: name, description, agent, model) + `steps/step-{NN}-{slug}.md` + `state.yaml` + optional `verify/` and helper scripts; `workflows/_active.yaml` is the in-flight index. All files use the `<!-- system:start -->…<!-- system:end -->` / `<!-- personal:start -->…<!-- personal:end -->` block structure.
- **Adding new capabilities is owned by Rigby** via `.claude/skills/rigby-capability-build/SKILL.md` (naming table, mandatory fairness-criteria check first, quality standards — every tool binding names exact files/commands; all changes tracked in `evolutions/.pending-changes.json`). Run `rigby-impact` before editing/deleting any existing capability. A new Amazing-Race-related skill or workflow (e.g., a Teams channel photo monitor) would follow exactly this structure — and per the Sept 30 error entries, any venue/location claims it makes must be verified, not drawn from model memory.
